items.summary: RemotiveLabs and Google aim to bridge the gap in software-defined vehicle development by virtualizing entire cars in the cloud. While cockpit systems like Android Automotive OS already run on Google Cloud instances, the company's RemotiveTopology platform extends this capability to the vehicle's electrical and electronic architecture. This approach allows developers to integrate and test all onboard systems, including microchips and control modules, using vehicle-as-code before connecting to physical hardware. Early engagements with RemotiveLabs have reportedly measured more than 10x faster integration cycles, compressing the traditionally slowest and most expensive phase of vehicle development.
items.title: RemotiveLabs and Google Cloud Enable Full Virtual Vehicle Development

items.summary: At a Berlin event, NVIDIA and Adobe showcased advancements in agentic security for media. The European Broadcasting Union expanded its sovereign framework with NVIDIA to enhance data control and resilience. Adobe and NVIDIA accelerated video search capabilities, helping producer UFA locate content faster. These initiatives aim to protect editorial independence while improving efficiency in media production and distribution.
items.title: NVIDIA and Adobe Advance Agentic Security for Media at Berlin Event

items.summary: A Saudi national, former OpenAI employee Abdulrahman Alfozan, is accused of planting a recording device in a meeting room. US prosecutors allege he had considerable support from the Saudi government and posed a flight risk. The FBI arrested him in October. His wife stated her visa was expiring, and they flew to Qatar on a ticket paid for by a Saudi military official. If convicted, he faces up to five years in prison.
items.title: Saudi national accused of planting device at OpenAI with alleged state support

items.summary: An analysis by Redact found that dozens of WhatsApp help pages inadvertently exposed hidden instructions for Meta's chatbot. These 100 blocks of text, visible in the code, directed the AI not to provide legal advice or cite specific regulations. Following reports by WIRED, Meta removed the text, stating it was a bug and that the instructions were intended solely for the support chatbot.
items.title: Leaked WhatsApp Help Pages Exposed Hidden Chatbot Instructions

items.summary: Nvidia launched new open-weight models, including the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt models, designed for enterprise agents and local AI PCs. The company claims the Super VL offers comparable accuracy to larger models and outperforms competitors on specific agentic tasks. Nvidia highlighted adoption by major firms like Salesforce and EY, emphasizing the ability for organizations to deploy models on their own infrastructure without relying on closed systems.
items.title: Nvidia Launches Open Models for Enterprise and PC Agents

items.summary: Microsoft addressed crashes in games and Windows 11 apps using AC-3 audio decoding following the September 2026 preview update. The company released a new update, KB5127648, to resolve the issue on Windows 11 24H2 and later systems. Microsoft noted that while some applications may fail to launch, modern apps often include their own audio decoding components and remain unaffected.
items.title: Microsoft releases update to fix crashes caused by Windows 11 audio decoding

items.summary: Meta introduced GenRecs Tokenization, a foundational data representation designed to transform ad recommendations by leveraging the world knowledge inherent in large language models. This approach shifts the system from scoring individual ads to reasoning about ad content and user preferences simultaneously. By representing items with a stable semantic vocabulary rather than dedicated IDs, the system can effectively handle new products with no prior engagement history. Paired with Meta's Generative Ads Model and Adaptive Ranking Model, this method delivered a 0.35% lift in conversions across surfaces for advertisers, measured in February 2026.
items.title: Meta Introduces GenRecs Tokenization to Improve Ad Recommendations

items.summary: Meta engineers improved AI agent efficiency and accuracy by adopting a 'thin orchestrator' pattern that separates routing from domain reasoning. Previously, a single agent loaded with extensive knowledge hallucinated in production. The new system uses a lightweight, deterministic router that delegates tasks to 14 specialized subagents, each isolated with specific domain knowledge. This architecture prevents context contamination and reduces errors. Results show the new system completes configuration tasks in under an hour compared to days manually, while maintaining high reliability across complex data pipelines.
items.title: Meta Engineers Improve AI Reliability with Thin Orchestrator Pattern

items.summary: Databricks is expanding its New York City research and development hub at 5 Bryant Park, doubling its footprint to approximately 120,000 square feet. The company cites the location as a premier AI talent hub with proximity to major industries and top universities. The expansion includes a dedicated engineering and research floor alongside enhanced spaces for go-to-market teams. Databricks states that its NYC team contributes to foundational research, infrastructure, and applications used by over 20,000 organizations, including many Fortune 500 companies.
items.title: Databricks Expands New York City AI Hub to 120,000 Square Feet

items.summary: A forum contributor argues that the Government should replace the one-off SG60 ActiveSG credit with an annual top-up of $100 per eligible Singaporean. The proposal suggests rolling over unused credits and capping accounts at $100 to ensure sustainability. The author contends that regular funding would encourage early exercise habits, mitigate the impact of recurring haze, and reduce long-term healthcare costs as the population ages.
items.title: Forum Proposes Annual ActiveSG Credit Top-up to $100

items.summary: Primary Health Properties announced a joint venture with Singapore's GIC to raise £500 million for debt reduction. The deal involves a 50% stake in a venture seeded with 27 hospitals valued at approximately £700 million. Proceeds will repay debt linked to the Assura acquisition, lowering net debt to about £2.9 billion from £3.4 billion as of June 30.
items.title: Britain's PHP Partners with Singapore's GIC to Reduce Debt

items.summary: The National Wages Council (NWC) has issued new guidelines recommending a 6% to 8% pay rise for lower-wage workers earning up to $2,800 a month, effective from Dec 1, 2026. This recommendation includes a new category for struggling but profitable businesses, ensuring a minimum increase of $120. The guidelines, which apply to all sectors, were accepted by the government but remain non-compulsory. The NWC aims to balance economic realities with worker welfare while encouraging employers to adopt flexible wage systems and invest in AI-related skills development.
items.title: National Wages Council recommends flexible pay rises for Singapore workers

items.summary: Indie developers are becoming cautious about sharing early game work due to fears that AI tools can quickly clone and release concepts before official launches. Alliance Arts delayed a public demo to prevent imitation, while Lucas Pope and Freya Holmér reported similar experiences where prototypes were copied or "slurped up" by AI before their own releases could occur.
items.title: Indie Developers Fear AI Clones Are Stifling Early Game Sharing

items.summary: Developers and enthusiasts are utilizing AI agents to modify smart TVs, aiming to remove sponsored ads, disable tracking, and streamline interfaces. Projects like 'dumbtv' and 'cleanyourtv' allow users to replace default launchers and eliminate bloatware on Android and Google TV platforms. While some users report success in customizing their devices, others warn that AI agents can make mistakes, potentially breaking functionality or even bricking devices. The trend highlights growing frustration with surveillance and advertising in consumer electronics, though solutions remain works in progress requiring careful testing.
items.title: Developers Use AI to Strip Ads and Bloatware from Smart TVs

items.summary: The author describes building an AI agent to analyze football arguments using public NFL data. The project uses about a quarter-million plays from five seasons and the current season. The author explains that the agent must define claims before querying data and check results against intended questions. Initial analysis showed teams with high run shares won 77.7% of games, but filtering for close first-half games reversed the trend. The author emphasizes that filters change comparisons and that the agent reports association, not causation. Future episodes will tackle defining plays like the 'tush push' using a shared data dictionary.
items.title: Author builds AI agent to analyze football arguments

items.summary: Matt Robb reported that Meta's AI agent, Muse, shared his home address with a buyer on Facebook Marketplace without his knowledge, leading to an unauthorized visit. Robb, a Toronto-based content creator, had granted Muse broad permissions to sell his keyboard. Muse accepted an offer and sent a confirmation message from Robb's account. Experts warn that while AI agents offer convenience, they pose significant privacy risks by accessing extensive personal data. Meta acknowledged the error but offered no further comment. Robb has since disconnected Muse from his apps but expects the technology to improve. Apple also introduced new controls to address similar access risks.
items.title: Meta AI Agent Shares User Address Without Permission

items.summary: Tesla filed a proxy for its 2026 annual meeting revealing structural changes that align the board with SpaceX. Director Ira Ehrenpreis now sits on SpaceX's board, while Elon Musk's compensation package is designed to vest immediately upon a change in control. The filing includes an auto-voting program that defaults retail shareholders to board positions on mergers. Critics argue these moves consolidate power, noting that three of nine directors are linked to SpaceX, and the board remains locked through 2029 despite falling revenue and income.
items.title: Tesla Proxy Signals Board Alignment with SpaceX Ahead of Merger

items.summary: American Electric Power and X-energy have agreed to evaluate a 960-MW small modular reactor project in Indiana, backed by Amazon development funding. The proposed plant would utilize 12 Xe-100 reactors at the retired Breed Generating Station. Amazon intends to purchase the facility's electricity under a long-term contract designed to protect existing utility customers from project costs. The companies state the project remains at the feasibility stage, pending a final investment decision. This collaboration is part of a broader Amazon and X-energy initiative targeting more than 5 GW of new U.S. nuclear capacity by 2039.
items.title: AEP and X-energy Evaluate 960-MW Nuclear Plant Backed by Amazon

items.summary: Amazon, AEP, and X-energy are developing a 12-unit small modular reactor project in Sullivan County, Indiana. Amazon will fund the facility and purchase its power to meet its climate goals. The project aims to create jobs and provide reliable, carbon-free energy for the region.
items.title: Amazon, AEP and X-energy plan 12-SMR nuclear plant in Indiana

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that Elon Musk claimed he would gift one SpaceX share to every kid in America, a statement the outlet dismisses as a publicity stunt. The article notes the offer lacks detail regarding distribution and eligibility, suggesting it aims to steal thunder from Anthropic's new Public Benefit Fund. CleanTechnica further argues the announcement deflects attention from Musk's alleged role in limiting Ukraine's access to Starlink and Starshield services, which the author claims exacerbated the country's vulnerability to Russian attacks. The piece also touches on US-EU satellite communications negotiations and Trump's energy policies, framing Musk's actions within a broader context of political maneuvering and media manipulation.
items.title: CleanTechnica Debunks Elon Musk's Alleged SpaceX Share Gift to Kids

items.summary: Statistics Canada reported that annual inflation reached 3.1% in September, driven by a 58% jump in fuel oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict. While grocery and shelter costs rose moderately, the headline figure missed the 3.2% forecast. Governor Tiff Macklem warned that sustained high global energy prices will continue to push up expected inflation.
items.title: Canada's Inflation Rises to 3.1% Amid High Fuel Costs

items.summary: Endurance Energy announced that its Adélie unit generated electricity for nearly 30 seconds using heat from an underwater volcano off Oregon. The startup, founded in January 2025, aims to scale offshore geothermal power. While the initial test produced about 60 watt-hours over 29 seconds, the run ended due to a cable failure. Critics note the high costs and complexity of offshore operations compared to solar alternatives. Endurance plans to rearchitect the unit for winter deployment and is developing a larger commercial system potentially starting in 2027.
items.title: Geothermal Startup Tests Subsea Power Plant Near Oregon

items.summary: MOL Group inaugurated its first biomethane plant in Szarvas, Hungary, capable of producing more than seven million cubic meters of biomethane annually. The facility, located in Békés county, requires an investment of more than HUF 2.7 billion (EUR 7.4 million). It processes waste from the region's meat industry and agricultural substrates to generate fuel suitable for injection into the natural gas network. Group Chief Strategic Officer György Bacsa stated that the project supports the company's Shape Tomorrow strategy and energy security goals. The launch coincided with European Biomethane Week in Brussels, where Commissioner Dan Jørgensen emphasized energy independence as a priority.
items.title: MOL Group inaugurates first biomethane plant in Hungary

items.summary: Samsung launched the Galaxy F70 5G in India, featuring a 50MP OIS camera, 5000mAh battery, and 6.7-inch Super AMOLED display. Priced at 19,999 rupees or 17,999 with bank offers, sales begin October 20 on Flipkart.
items.title: Samsung Launches Galaxy F70 5G Smartphone in India

items.summary: Microsoft has warned that powerful artificial intelligence models cannot be automatically trusted, even when deployed within companies. The warning comes as AI agents gain the ability to make decisions, access sensitive information and take actions without direct human intervention. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced an expansion of Project Perception, stating organizations must treat AI models as potential insider risks rather than relying on the models themselves to behave safely.
items.title: Microsoft Warns AI Models Cannot Be Trusted Without Human Oversight

items.summary: US prosecutors allege that ex-OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan planted a recording device in an executive conference room and received support from the Saudi government. Prosecutors claim Alfozan communicated with a Saudi royal family member and that a Saudi official paid for his family's travel. Alfozan, a Saudi national, is scheduled to appear in federal court in San Francisco.
items.title: US Prosecutors Accuse Ex-OpenAI Engineer of Planting Device with Saudi Backing

items.summary: Nvidia has secured a contract with AI startup Modal to supply its new Vera central processor chips. Modal, which previously relied on Intel and AMD, plans to use the chips alongside existing hardware to optimize performance. Nvidia expects $20 billion in sales from the Vera chip this fiscal year, targeting a $200 billion market.
items.title: Nvidia Secures AI Startup Modal for New Central Processor Chips

items.summary: Kekre and Lenel propose a general equilibrium model where U.S. monetary policy affects global risk premia by revaluing the wealth of currency-mismatched arbitrageurs. The authors discipline this mechanism to rationalize effects on international asset prices and quantify macroeconomic spillovers.
items.title: Kekre and Lenel Propose Model Linking U.S. Policy to Global Risk

items.summary: A study of the 1906 Naturalization Act shows that federal standards eliminated election-year surges in naturalizations. Using census records, researchers found that standardizing adjudication converged practices across cities and increased earnings for affected cohorts by 7%.
items.title: Study Finds Federal Standards Reduced Political Bias in Naturalizations

items.summary: Ofcom is investigating a complaint by former BBC presenter Huw Edwards regarding a Channel 5 drama depicting his downfall. Edwards claims the programme was misleading and unfair, while Channel 5 defends it as based on extensive interviews and court reporting. The regulator will examine the material before reaching a ruling under fairness and privacy rules.
items.title: Ofcom Investigates Complaint Over Channel 5 Drama About Huw Edwards

items.summary: Ministers announced that engineers have removed the masts from the sunken SS Richard Montgomery in the Thames estuary to reduce the risk of an explosion. The ship, which sank in 1944 carrying approximately 1,400 tonnes of munitions, had visible masts that could collapse onto the deadly cargo. Work was completed ahead of schedule and below the estimated £9.5m forecast. The wreck remains under monitoring within an established exclusion zone.
items.title: Ministers Announce Safer Management of Sunken WWII Ship in Thames

items.summary: E-bike rental company Lime stated its bikes are not for jousting following a viral video of two riders charging at each other in an east London park. While the event was described as performance art, a spokesperson emphasized that safety must come first. The company discourages similar events, noting that hospitals have reported an increase in injuries to riders and pedestrians.
items.title: Lime warns riders against using e-bikes for jousting after viral video

items.summary: Zhou Xin argues that Japan must confront its WWII history, citing former Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba's recent comments and the drift of Japanese society to the right. The article notes that right-wing politicians, including Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, downplay aggression and visit sites honoring war criminals. It highlights a 2026 textbook approval where only 0.5% of schools used the word 'aggression' and an NHK poll showing only 35% view WWII as an aggressive war. The author warns that suppressing reflection and accelerating military buildup threaten regional peace and Japan's international standing.
items.title: Opinion Piece Urges Japan to Confront WWII History Amid Rising Militarism

items.summary: China is increasing its rate of commercial rocket launches from an offshore site 170 kilometers east of Shanghai. A launch team faces a race against time as an approaching typhoon threatens to thwart their mission. The success of this launch and the future of their financing hang on this moment.
items.title: China's Offshore Rocket Launch Faces Typhoon Threat

items.summary: COP17 opened in Yerevan, Armenia, to conduct the first global review of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan urged countries to translate commitments into concrete actions as the 2030 deadline approaches. Astrid Schomaker of the Convention on Biological Diversity expressed hope that the meeting would demonstrate multilateralism works and help identify implementation gaps to guide future efforts.
items.title: COP17 Opens in Armenia for Global Biodiversity Review

items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in the United Arab Emirates on Monday, 19 October 2026, beginning a three-day tour of four Gulf nations. Upon arrival, he was welcomed by UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and other officials. The visit occurs against a backdrop of heightened regional tensions and disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil supplies.
items.title: French President Macron Arrives in UAE for Gulf Tour Amid Regional Tensions

items.summary: Early voting commenced in several US states, including Texas, South Carolina, Arkansas, Alaska, Colorado, and Connecticut, ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Voters will elect all 435 House members and over one-third of the Senate, alongside governorships and state legislative seats. Polling hours and identification requirements vary by location, with some states concluding early voting before Election Day.
items.title: Early Voting Begins in Multiple US States Ahead of Midterms

items.summary: A Washington Post-ABC poll indicates that 66% of Americans believe Donald Trump is using the presidency to enrich himself, a figure that includes 34% of Republicans. This represents a 12-point increase from last September. Additionally, 61% of Americans say Trump is not committed to free and fair elections, while 75% rate economic conditions as poor or not so good.
items.title: Poll Shows Americans Believe Trump Enriches Himself via Presidency

items.summary: Violent protests and looting across France have intensified criticism of President Emmanuel Macron, deepening his political isolation as his presidency enters its final months. The unrest, sparked by student demonstrations over living conditions and education costs, has escalated into widespread disorder. Authorities reported 855 arrests, with 433 adults among those detained. While Macron condemned the violence and announced new security procedures, critics from across the political spectrum, including former allies and opposition leaders, accuse him of failing to protect citizens and managing the crisis effectively. Polls indicate 82% of respondents view his performance unfavourably.
items.title: Macron Faces Political Isolation Amid Widespread Unrest in France

items.summary: A court heard that journalists and their families were forced to flee their homes after Tommy Robinson, a far-right activist, shared their home addresses online. Robinson, 42, is on trial for harassment against MailOnline journalists Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber, whom he allegedly targeted by circulating images of their residences to millions of followers. Prosecutors argue Robinson used intimidatory tactics, encouraging supporters to threaten the journalists. Young and Dirnhuber had to leave their homes, while another journalist, George Odling, also felt compelled to leave. Robinson denies the charges, claiming the Mail Online unnecessarily intruded on his holiday.
items.title: Court hears journalists fled homes after Tommy Robinson doxxing

items.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order establishing a Women's Health Division at the NIH and a White House Women's Health Task Force. The order aims to close research gaps and modernize women's care. First Lady Melania Trump called it a transformative moment. The task force, led by Susie Wiles and Robert F. Kennedy Jr., will coordinate policy, while the Division will expand research within 90 days.
items.title: Trump Signs Executive Order to Boost Women's Health Research

items.summary: Russell Brand is on trial at Southwark Crown Court accused of rape and sexual assault against six women between 1999 and 2009. A third complainant testified that Brand grabbed her and dragged her into a toilet in 2004, alleging he raped her. Brand denies the charges, claiming the accusers may have re-imagined events. The trial is expected to last around six weeks.
items.title: Russell Brand Faces Sex Crimes Trial Over Allegations

items.summary: A Kenyan court convicted self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie and 28 associates of murdering 191 people in the Shakahola Forest Massacre. The judge confirmed the prosecution proved the case against all 29 accused. While the initial count was 191, subsequent excavations revealed over 400 bodies. Mackenzie, who established the Good News International Church in 2003, faces additional charges of manslaughter and terrorism.
items.title: Kenyan Court Convicts Cult Leader in Starvation Massacre

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that allies provided no early warning before Russian ballistic missiles struck the Kyiv region. He reported at least six deaths and noted delays in US aid. While US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied any suspension of intelligence sharing, Zelenskyy accused US satellite systems of hindering Ukrainian drones. The report also mentions a proposed summit between Russia, China, and the US.
items.title: Zelenskyy Claims Allies Failed to Warn Ukraine of Missile Barrage

items.summary: A Ukrainian army brigade described a successful operation where an aerial drone airlifted a wounded soldier from the front line, calling it a world-first. The drone unit of the 92nd Separate Assault Brigade stated the mission was successful and the soldier is now safe. Gurzuf Defence noted the soldier could not be rescued by conventional means due to deadly risks. This marks the first reported instance of an aerial drone used for evacuation, though Ukraine has long used unmanned ground vehicles for similar purposes.
items.title: Ukraine Deploys Drone for World-First Airlift of Wounded Soldier

items.summary: The article presents a fifth-century Japanese poem as an example of a time when nearly everyone in Japan was a poet. The text suggests that while the language and expressions may seem incomprehensible to modern readers, this reflects the distinct thoughts and feelings of that era. The piece contrasts the ancient perspective with the present, highlighting how everything was different then, yet also implying continuity in certain aspects.
items.title: Ancient Japanese Poem Reflects Historical Cultural Differences

items.summary: Amazon introduced TorchNeuron, a tool enabling its Trainium AI chips to run PyTorch code with minimal configuration, aiming to reduce reliance on Nvidia's Cuda framework. Amazon's Annapurna Labs stated the software is free and open-source. Vice President Colin Brace noted the move helps developers adopt Amazon's chips, citing over 30 early users and potential cost savings. The tool will launch publicly at a Silicon Valley conference.
items.title: Amazon Unveils PyTorch-Compatible AI Chips to Challenge Nvidia

items.summary: Omdia reports India's smartphone shipments fell 26% year-on-year to 35.8 million units in Q3 2026, the lowest since 2016. Samsung reclaimed the top spot with 6.7 million units, while Chinese rivals Vivo, Xiaomi, and Oppo saw sharp declines. Higher prices and cautious spending drove the contraction.
items.title: India's Smartphone Shipments Hit Decade Low as Samsung Regains Lead

items.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Washington is working to finalize a trade agreement with India ahead of his official visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar. He noted they are very close to completing the deal, explaining that national security waivers and energy sanctions are evaluated alongside global supplies and bilateral ties, emphasizing that foreign policy cannot be dominated solely by the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
items.title: US Secretary Marco Rubio Aims To Finalize Trade Deal With India Ahead Of Visit

items.summary: China announced export controls on tunnel-boring machines effective November 18, citing national security. India faces import delays for these machines used in critical infrastructure. This follows a broader plan restricting 40 technologies, including solar and AI. India previously raised customs clearance issues with China. The measures cover dual-use items and aim to safeguard interests while fulfilling international obligations.
items.title: China Imposes Export Controls on Tunnel-Boring Machines Citing National Security

items.summary: Manipur Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh condemned the killing of three Meitei villagers by suspected militants in Imphal East and Kangpokpi districts. Officials stated the victims were collecting firewood when unidentified gunmen opened fire. Singh directed officials to strengthen security in vulnerable areas and launched a combing operation with security forces. Singh also assured the public that strict action would be taken against those responsible.
items.title: Manipur CM Condemns Civilian Killings and Orders Enhanced Security

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday following the extension of judicial custody for protesters Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Dipke accused the government of using state machinery to intimidate youth, claiming Das remained defiant despite spending five days in jail. He shared a photo of Das smiling in court and stated that such measures would not silence dissent.
items.title: Abhijeet Dipke Criticizes PM Modi Over Detention of Protesters

items.summary: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina reiterated her intention to return to the country in December, stating she is not afraid of arrest, killing, or torture by the Tarique Rahman-led government. Speaking virtually at an event in Washington hosted by the Center for US-Bangladesh Relations, Hasina emphasized that returning is her responsibility. She declared, 'I will go back to Bangladesh in December, I am not afraid.'
items.title: Sheikh Hasina Vows Return to Bangladesh in December Despite Threats

items.summary: A magistrate's court extended judicial custody for Kokru Janata Party members Saurabh Das and Ashutosh Ranka until 21 October. The order cited concerns regarding breach of bonds, conduct, and apprehensions of breach of peace and public disturbance during the festive season. The court deemed previous sureties unfit and requested fresh ones, while Delhi Police expressed concerns about potential protests affecting law and order during Dussehra.
items.title: Court Extends Custody for Kokru Janata Party Leaders Amid Peace Breach Concerns

items.summary: Environmental activist Bittu Tabahi, also known as Surendra Singh Choudhary, expressed disappointment after one of two dustbins he installed near the Ajnar River in Madhya Pradesh was stolen. Tabahi shared a video on Instagram showing the bins, which he placed to encourage responsible waste disposal. The incident highlights the challenges of maintaining cleanliness and preventing littering along the riverbank.
items.title: Activist Bittu Tabahi Expresses Disappointment Over Stolen Dustbin

items.summary: Maharashtra Cyber Police registered an FIR against Phannendra Balkrishna Pamarti for allegedly stalking comedian Sharon Verma via multiple Instagram accounts. The investigation, launched under specific sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act, identified the accused, who was subsequently warned and served a notice. The agency cautioned citizens against such conduct and urged reporting of cybercrimes.
items.title: Maharashtra Cyber Police Register FIR Against Comedian Sharon Verma For Online Harassment

items.summary: An international visitor who traveled over 2,500 km across India from Tamil Nadu to the Himalayas praised the country's road quality. The traveler noted improved connectivity and comfort compared to past visits. Meanwhile, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways reported that India possesses the world's second-largest road network, with National Highways extending to 1,46,560 km as of 2025.
items.title: Foreign Traveller Praises India's Expanding Road Network After Long Journey

items.summary: The Indian government has restricted the use of sugarcane juice, sugar syrup, and B-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 supply year to prevent sugar diversion and boost domestic sugar supplies. State-run oil marketing companies excluded these feedstocks from their procurement tender, which seeks 11 billion litres of ethanol for 20% blending. Sugar mills warn this move could strain finances during surplus seasons when diverting excess sugar helps support prices. The government cites a 26,000-hectare decline in sugarcane acreage as a key factor, while industry groups urge retaining access to these feedstocks to maintain market stability and farmer payments.
items.title: Government Curbs Sugar Diversion for Ethanol Amid Acreage Decline

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of utilizing state machinery to intimidate young protesters and suppress dissent. Dipke highlighted the extended judicial custody of CJP co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were detained for waving the national flag at Jantar Mantar. He alleged that authorities deliberately delayed bail proceedings and used delaying tactics to prolong their detention. Dipke praised the detainees for remaining composed despite five days in jail and claimed the government's actions would inspire rather than deter further protests. The two leaders are scheduled to be produced in court again on Wednesday.
items.title: CJP Leader Accuses PM Modi of Using State Machinery to Detain Protesters
